intro.author: Traditionally Moses. The book itself names no author, and many scholars think it was shaped from several earlier sources over time.
intro.written: Traditionally during Israel's years in the wilderness; many scholars date its final form much later, in the time of the kings or after the exile.
intro.audience: The people of Israel, learning where the world, the nations and their own family came from
intro.setting: Genesis opens before history begins and closes with Jacob's family living in Egypt. Its first eleven chapters cover the whole world; the rest follow one family, from Abraham to his great-grandson Joseph, as they move among the cities and grazing lands of Mesopotamia, Canaan and Egypt.
intro.purpose: To tell how the one God made a good world, how human sin damaged it, and how God began a plan to bless all nations through Abraham's family.
intro.bigIdea: God creates, people rebel, and God keeps his promises anyway.

outline.title: Creation, the fall, the flood and Babel
